subject: Final-mile MAP: deployment mode + region decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai

Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-08-21 09:12 -0700
Subject: Final-mile MAP: deployment mode + region decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Emma — thanks again for yesterday's call. Quick summary and proposed next steps so we can land the MAP and pick a deployment lane that meets Pioneer’s data residency and latency needs.

Key milestones (proposed):
- Week 1 (Aug 24–28): finalize hosting choice + sign SOW (you + procurement)
- Week 2 (Aug 31–Sep 4): PoC kickoff (dedicated test pool, EU region)
- Weeks 3–4: acceptance tests, performance/latency evaluation, security checklist verification

Options we discussed (pros/cons short):
- Hosted (fastest onramp): low ops, global footprint. Pros: speed, lower initial cost. Cons: not ideal for strict EU-only residencies unless we use private tenancy + data geofencing.
- Dedicated (recommended for Pioneer): reserved EU GPU pools, customer data isolation, optional KMS/HSM integration. Pros: predictable throughput, can meet SOC2 / data residency. Cons: higher committed cost.
- Private/on-prem: full control, air-gapped if needed. Pros: compliance highest. Cons: longest lead time and ops overhead.

Ask: Can you confirm by EOD next Tue (Aug 25) whether Pioneer wants to proceed with Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private so we can circulate an SOW and schedule procurement? I attached the MAP_v1.xlsx with milestones and owner assignments.

If Dedicated looks right, we’ll surface a draft SOW + ballpark pricing and an EU PoC plan by Monday.

Thanks —
Jonas Weber
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Attachment: MAP_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, MAP milestones)

Subject: Re: Final-mile MAP: deployment mode + region decision (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private)

Thanks Jonas — the summary is helpful. A few points from our side:
- Pioneer is subject to strict EU data residency for PHI-like telemetry; our legal team is pushing for either Dedicated in EU or a Private deployment. Hosted with geo-tagging is likely insufficient for our auditors.
- Security asks: can Redwood support customer-managed KMS/HSM, detailed key rotation logs, and an exportable audit trail for token-level access? We’ll need SOC2-type evidence and a short list of controls for procurement.
- Cost: please send a ballpark committed vs pay-as-you-go estimate for Dedicated (3-month PoC and 12-month reserved).
- PoC scope: we want 100k tokens/day simulated traffic, latency targets p95 < 250ms in EU-1, and a short evaluation script (we can provide sample prompts).

If you can get back with the SOW + security evidence early next week that would be perfect. I looped Raj (procurement) in case we need to move quickly.

Best,
Emma Burns
VP Product | Pioneer Health

Emma — quick update and concrete proposal after internal sync:
- Recommendation: Dedicated (EU) with optional customer-managed KMS. Based on your audit note, Hosted’s geo-tagging doesn’t give the evidence pack auditors want. Dedicated allows us to provide the isolation and auditability you need while keeping the onramp timeline short.
- Security: we can support external KMS (Bring Your Own Key) via our KMS bridge; full key-rotation logs and exportable audit trails will be included in the evidence pack. SOC2 artifacts attached as part of the pack.
- Pricing (ballpark):
  - 3-month PoC (dedicated test pool, limited throughput): €12,000 (one-time setup + monthly reserved credit)
  - 12-month reserved (production): €28,000/month (committed capacity for peak 250rps)
  - Note: we can propose a blended ramp discount for the first 6 months if Pioneer commits to 12 months.
- PoC plan (proposed dates):
  - Aug 31: PoC kickoff (provisioned EU dedicated pool)
  - Sep 01–10: performance and latency tests (we’ll run your evaluation script)
  - Sep 11–18: security checklist validation & audit artifacts handoff
  - Sep 20: acceptance decision and provisioning for production lane

Attached: Draft_SOW_jonas_v2.pdf — it includes the Dedicated EU configuration, KMS checkbox, and acceptance criteria. I’ve also added a DocuSign link for a one-click SOW approval.

If this aligns, I’ll send a version with Raj/Procurement in the To field and drop the DocuSign.

Cheers —
Jonas
Attachment: Draft_SOW_jonas_v2.pdf (PDF, SOW draft)
